aspect.evidence: the track's stored width and height

transfer.limit: a transfer curve is named, not verified against the pixels

faceCoverage.evidence: his face was readable in 209 of 209 frames read (0 none found, 0 too dark to read, 0 too small for the landmarks to mean anything)

position.evidence: the median of his eye-line over the frames his face was read in

travel.evidence: the 5th-to-95th-percentile span of his eye-line, so one lost frame does not set it

scale.evidence: median eye distance over frame height

reach.evidence: median distance from his eye-line to the bottom of frame, in eye-distances

coverage.evidence: a reach of 11.4743 eye-distances read against ordinary human proportion
coverage.limit: a rule of thumb about bodies, not a measurement of this one; a crouch or a low camera will move it

faceNearEdge.evidence: his eye-line against a band 8 % in from each edge
faceNearEdge.limit: his FACE only. Where his hands, elbows and shoulders are is not read here, so a body that leaves frame will not show up in this finding

unsteadySteps.evidence: border movement above 0.004 of frame width, over 208 steps

stability.evidence: 0 % of steps moved, worst 0 of frame width
stability.limit: a threshold on whole-pixel matching at 64 cells across: a slow push smaller than one cell reads as locked

motionSource.evidence: the frame's border is taken to be background and the whole frame to include him; the two are compared
motionSource.limit: no optical flow and no depth: a camera that pans while he walks the other way is not resolved, and is reported as mixed or cannot_separate rather than guessed

drift.evidence: the sum of border movement over the stretch
drift.limit: accumulated whole-cell steps; it drifts with its own rounding and is an indication of direction, not a displacement

exposure.evidence: median frame brightness and its 5th-to-95th-percentile span

clipping.evidence: share of pixels at or beyond the ends of the range, median over frames

colourCast.evidence: mean of each channel over every cell of every frame

keyDirection.evidence: a brightness difference of 0.0356 across and 0.2705 down the picture
keyDirection.limit: where the picture is brighter, not where a lamp is. A bright wall on one side reads the same as a key from that side, and this cannot tell them apart

softness.evidence: a left-to-right brightness difference of 0.3326 across the band he stands in, with 0.0112 of the picture clipped
softness.limit: UNCALIBRATED — no shadow edge is found and no light is measured. It reads how much the light models HIM, at the resolution of a 12-cell grid, which a wall behind him also contributes to. Treat it as a hint, never as a lighting spec

peakSharpness.evidence: median over frames of the sharpest tile in each
peakSharpness.limit: a number for this clip only. It is not comparable with another clip of a different size, bitrate or codec

blurredFrames.evidence: frames whose sharpest tile falls below 0.6 of this clip's median

subjectVsBackground.evidence: sharpness in the tiles around his face against tiles 3 or more away
subjectVsBackground.limit: the tiles he stands in are guessed from his FACE, not from a cut-out of him. A hand waved into a background tile, or a chair beside him, lands in the wrong half

depthOfField.limit: says which is sharper, not an aperture and not a distance. A flat wall behind him reads as soft because there is nothing in it to be sharp

difficulty.evidence: 1 of the four things that make a cut-out hard are present
difficulty.limit: a reading of the picture, not an attempt at a matte. Hair, a cap's brim, a chain and anything reflective are the usual failures and are NOT measured here — no matte was pulled

reasons: the background carries a lot of detail, which a matte has to follow rather than flood

edgeContrast.evidence: brightness difference between the column he stands in and the columns two cells either side

feetVisible.evidence: a reach of 11.4743 eye-distances, against 24 for a whole standing body
feetVisible.limit: inferred from where his eyes are and where the frame ends. Nothing here sees a foot: a crouch, a low camera or a step towards the lens all break it

contactNeeded.evidence: the frame ends above his feet, so there is no contact point to match and no contact shadow to invent
contactNeeded.limit: about whether a contact is NEEDED, not whether AVT can make one

lipSyncJudgeable.evidence: a take is the reference, so there is nothing to hold it against
lipSyncJudgeable.limit: lip sync is a comparison between a clip and the take it was made from (storyboard/takeCheck.ts). It cannot be judged from one file alone, and this analysis does not try

notEstablished: the lighting's geometry — how many sources, where they stand, how far, how large
focal length, aperture, sensor size, camera height and the distance to anything in frame
how a matte actually behaves on his hair, the brim of his cap, and anything reflective he is wearing — nothing here pulls one
anything about sound or sync — the file carries no audio track

hard.text: Leave the performer's place clear: his eye-line sits at 51 % across and 34 % down the frame. Put nothing of interest there, and nothing that has to be read behind his head and shoulders.
He moves across 41 % of the frame and 3 % down it. Keep that band clear of anything the eye has to follow.
The camera does not move. The background must be locked off too — any drift in it will read as the room sliding behind a man who is standing still.
Mean brightness is 0.53 of full scale. Build the background to that, not brighter: he cannot be relit.
The take carries a colour cast (r 0.53 g 0.51 b 0.44). Grade the background to it rather than correcting him.
The file is tagged arib-std-b67. A background generated in ordinary sRGB will not match it until one of the two is converted, and converting him is what loses his skin.
The background must be delivered at 1080 × 1920 or larger. Anything smaller has to be scaled up into him.
Do not reframe wider or lower than the take. There is no footage of his legs or feet; a background that reveals them will reveal nothing.

preferences.text: The take frames him thigh up. A background built for a fuller figure will not match: there is no footage of the rest of him.
The brighter side of the picture is above. Light the background from the same side; a background keyed from the opposite side is the single most visible mismatch in a composite.
His light reads medium. Match that: a background lit flatter than he is will look pasted behind him.
The background is about as sharp as he is: a defocused plate will read as a different lens.
A matte is workable but not free; keep the background away from his edges in brightness and detail.
The frame ends above his feet, so no floor contact and no contact shadow has to be matched — one fewer thing for the background to get wrong.

because: the camera is locked and he separates from the background well enough that a plate can go behind him
his performance, timing and lip movement survive a composite exactly, which is the thing a restaging kept failing
risks: AVT cannot pull the matte this needs today — see gaps

rejected.why: a generative restage re-renders his performance; this take does not need that risk
nothing in the footage is unusable

capture: The take frames him thigh up. If a shot may ever want him fuller, film it fuller — a crop can take away, nothing can add.
This take carries no sound. Record audio even when the music is added later: it is what sync is measured against.
gaps: AVT has no colour-transfer step: nothing in the pipeline converts arib-std-b67 footage to the space a generated plate is produced in, or back
AVT has no matte step for ordinary footage: scripts/edit/composite_environment.py composites against a plate with hand-set occluder bands, and nothing pulls a per-frame matte of him
